question: Which of the following correctly pairs a first-line anti-tuberculosis drug with its primary mechanism of action?

answers.text: Isoniazid — inhibits mycolic acid synthesis by blocking InhA (enoyl-ACP reductase)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Isoniazid is a prodrug activated by mycobacterial KatG (catalase-peroxidase). The active metabolite forms an adduct with NAD that inhibits InhA, blocking mycolic acid synthesis — essential for the mycobacterial cell wall.

answers.text: Rifampicin — inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding PBPs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PBP binding is the mechanism of beta-lactams. Rifampicin inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase (the beta subunit), blocking mRNA synthesis.

answers.text: Ethambutol — inhibits DNA gyrase, preventing DNA supercoiling

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: DNA gyrase inhibition is the mechanism of fluoroquinolones. Ethambutol inhibits arabinosyl transferase, disrupting arabinogalactan synthesis in the mycobacterial cell wall.

answers.text: Pyrazinamide — inhibits 50S ribosomal subunit, halting protein synthesis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 50S inhibition is the mechanism of macrolides. Pyrazinamide (as pyrazinoic acid) disrupts the mycobacterial membrane potential and inhibits fatty acid synthase I, active specifically in acidic/hypoxic environments.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the First-Line ATT Drugs block. Each of HRZE targets a distinct mycobacterial structure: INH→mycolic acid, RIF→RNA pol, EMB→arabinogalactan, PZA→membrane/FAS-I.
Excellent. Knowing HRZE mechanisms helps explain their complementary coverage of different bacterial populations and their distinct toxicity profiles.
